expectations.text: Asks the expert numbered clarifying questions in at least 2 rounds before presenting contexts
expectations.evidence: Message 1 asks numbered questions 1-6; message 2 asks numbered follow-ups 1-5; the context list is first presented in message 3.

expectations.text: An independent critic reviewed the contexts and, separately, the context map per business process
expectations.evidence: No critic or reviewer agent appears anywhere in the transcript or final message. The only check mentioned is 'No upstream/downstream loops (checked with tsort)'. No per-process walkthrough of the map.

expectations.text: Asks the expert for approval of the contexts before building the map
expectations.evidence: Message 3 presents the context list and asks 'Is that right? Anything misplaced?'; expert: 'the list of contexts is right'. Message 4 adds TutorSearch and asks 'Does that still match how you work?'; expert: 'With these two changes I'm happy with the list.' The map is only produced in message 5. Note: the map itself was never shown for approval, and the expert was never asked which processes to check or whether a CML map is wanted.

notes:
Map quality vs trainer rules: weak on relationship patterns. Every internal relationship is [U,PL|OHS]->[D,CF]: downstream Conformist to internal teams' languages everywhere, no ACL on any internal downstream, and no Customer/Supplier even though the expert said all teams are in one company (the run never asked about team relationships). This violates 'ACL default', 'C/S between internal teams' and 'CF only to well-established languages'. Positives: no Shared Kernel; CF to Stripe and ACL to the video provider are correct; no U/D cycles (verified with tsort), achieved by making LessonDelivery an OHS service called by Scheduling and by asking the expert to confirm - a cleaner cycle resolution than the with_skill run's kept indirect cycle. It also explicitly proposed breaking a loop by removing Pricing from Scheduling, the expert rejected it, and it found another fix - good behaviour.

Context split: matches ground truth on all four key boundaries. Extras: TutorSearch modelled as a context although the expert said it has no rules (created only to break a cycle - questionable; a read model would do), Notifications as a context (improvised, no rules), TutorProfiles as a separate context with the rate. No subdomain classification, no canvases, no discovery report, no map approval, no process walkthroughs (did not ask for the expert's processes).

Cost: ~79k tokens, ~4 min, 4 expert rounds - much cheaper. For the skill, the comparison shows the skill's real value is in relationship patterns (C/S+ACL), critic catches (50% ownership) and traceable artifacts, not in the context split itself, which the baseline gets right. Assertions 1-5 and 7 do not discriminate between runs; only assertion 6 does.
